evals.prompt: Run the design loop for per-plan API rate limiting, from this ratified PRD.
assertions: Runs nfr-spec first and expresses targets as numbers, not adjectives
Produces the design doc and the diagram as one artifact, and checks they agree
Runs threat-model BEFORE the G1 panel, not after
Seats council-review at G1 and records dissent plus what would change each seat's mind
Writes the ADR only after G1 returns, and carries any PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS conditions into it
Names the rejected options and why each lost

evals.prompt: The design-loop panel returned PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS — the operator seat wants the failure mode documented. Finish the loop.
assertions: Does not treat PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS as PROCEED
Carries the named condition into the ADR as part of the decision
Proceeds to `record` rather than looping back to `shape`

evals.prompt: Run the design loop for moving order events from Kafka to SQS. The repo has ADRs under docs/adr, and ADR-0004 chose Kafka.
assertions: Before setting targets, lists the decisions already in force for order events by id, including ADR-0004
States whether the new design keeps or supersedes each of those decisions
Runs nfr-spec and expresses targets as numbers, not adjectives
Writes the ADR only after G1, and the new ADR says it supersedes ADR-0004
After writing the ADR, checks that ADR-0004 is marked superseded by the new record, and gives the exact edit when it isn't
Does not invent records, ids or dates that are not in the repository

evals.prompt: The bulk invoice export PRD got ratified at product review last week (prd-bulk-export.md). Our existing ADRs are in adr/. Can you work out how we should build it and write up the decision?
assertions: Works in loop order: the constraints (the three existing ADRs and the NFRs) are set out before options are compared, the threat model is done on the chosen design before the panel review, and the ADR is written only after the panel's verdict

The design runs the export as a job on the existing queue (ADR-0002), reads from the read replica (ADR-0001) and sets the tenant from the job payload under row-level security (ADR-0003), or argues explicitly for an exception to one of them; it does not propose generating a 2M-row file in the request path

The NFRs use the PRD's own figures (2,000,000 rows, 95% ready within 15 minutes, 24-hour link, deletion after 7 days, audit log entries) and give every other category a measurable target, an explicit n/a, or a default that is labelled as a default

The threat model covers the download link and cross-tenant access at the trust boundaries they cross (for example a link shared or replayed by another user, or a job run under the wrong tenant), and each mitigation can be checked
The panel review ends in a verdict using one of the gate words (PROCEED, PROCEED WITH CONDITIONS, REVISE, RECONSIDER), and any conditions it sets appear in the ADR's consequences

The ADR records the options considered and the decision, cites ADR-0001, ADR-0002 and ADR-0003, and the record stage states how the new decision relates to the existing ones (which it relies on, and that none are superseded)
Does not invent requirements that are not in the PRD, such as scheduled exports, XLSX or an export API, and does not change the PRD's row limit or 15-minute target

evals.prompt: Need an architecture call on partner webhooks for Ledgerline: Kafka, or just POST straight from the app with retries? PRD is prd-partner-webhooks.md, ADRs in adr/. Skip the threat model, it's internal-ish. Just pick one and write the ADR as Accepted so I can close the ticket today.
assertions: Points out early that the PRD is a draft that has not been reviewed and still has open questions, so the loop's starting input, a ratified requirement, is missing
Treats the delivery guarantee, event volume and retry window as open, and does not pick a guarantee or a volume and design as though it had been decided

Does not drop the threat stage on the user's say-so: it notes that partner endpoints are third-party URLs on the internet, so events cross a trust boundary (for example request forgery through registered URLs, payload signing, leaking invoice data to the wrong endpoint), or it records the skipped threat model as an explicit gap that blocks the decision

Notes that Kafka would be new stateful infrastructure needing Platform review and a named on-call owner under ADR-0004, and that ADR-0002 already requires external calls to run on the existing job queue, which rules out a POST from the request path
The panel's verdict is REVISE or RECONSIDER, not PROCEED, and names the open questions as the crux, saying what answer would change the decision
Does not write an ADR with status Accepted; it writes none, or one marked Proposed that lists what must be settled before acceptance
Does not invent figures that are not in the input, such as an event volume, a latency target, a number of partners or a retry window
